relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: unpaid mailboxes whose DFY order was refunded cannot be paid from the billing page (no managed domains shown)
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Intercom conversation

<url:app.intercom.com>

## Conversation context

Same Intercom thread as ENG-14509. On 2026-10-05 the customer (owner of the Company Two workspace) wrote: "The profile says review billing, and when we go in everything is in order, how do we resume the campaign?" Support answered that the campaign was active and not paused, then said "It seems that your payment for the inboxes did not go through. Kindly revisit your payment." Asked to check the Company Two workspace specifically, the customer replied "The payment date is only the 10th?" and, after support confirmed, asked: "Then how would the inbox payment not have gone through?"

## Testable claim

In the Company Two workspace, the 3 mailboxes on <domain> are flagged unpaid with a 6 October cancellation date, but the billing page lists no managed domains for that workspace, so the owner has no resubscribe control to pay for them and cannot act on the notice.

## Evidence

* Production audit row for the workspace: domain <domain>, payment_state 'unpaid' and open (no resolved_at, no dismissed_at) since 2026-09-10, held_domains 1, held_inboxes 3, paid_domains 0, paid_inboxes 0, mail_domain_status 'failed', note "Inboxes unpaid (aggregate)".
* The same row's order_id is a DFY domain purchase order whose status is 'refunded' (refunded 2026-08-11 after the provider failed to provision it; refundableDomains 1, refundableInboxes 3, retriesExhausted true).
* The workspace's only mail_domain row is that domain, status 'failed'. The provider-side mailbox subscription is still ACTIVE with auto-renew and period end 2026-10-11, and the 3 mailboxes exist and are 'active' in the app, so the workspace keeps sending from them.
* listManagedDomains filters out mail domains whose purchase order status is 'refunded' (and whose domain status is 'suspended'), so the managed list for this workspace is empty. EmailAccountsDomainsCard returns its "No managed domains" empty state before rendering the "Review and resubscribe" and per-domain "Resubscribe" controls, which are the only entry points to the pay-unpaid-mailboxes flow. The customer is an owner of the workspace, so the pay flow itself is available to her; it is simply unreachable from the page.
* Blast radius counted 2026-10-05: 4 organizations and 9 open 'unpaid' findings whose purchase order is refunded (query joined cmr_domain_audit_finding to domain_purchase_order on order_id, filtered payment_state 'unpaid', resolved_at and dismissed_at null, order status 'refunded').
* Two reminder emails for the unpaid mailboxes were sent on 2026-09-29 to <email> and <email>, which puts the notice's cancellation date at 2026-10-06 (7-day grace).
* The customer's report matches the code path: the billing page shows her nothing to pay.

## Code

* apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts, listManagedDomains (the ne(domainPurchaseOrderTable.status, 'refunded') filter).
* apps/web/components/billing/email-accounts-domains-card.tsx, EmailAccountsDomainsCard (empty-state early return hides the resubscribe controls).

relatedSnapshot.title: Investigate billing for pending & errored ColdMailReseller inboxes
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Summary

We currently have **3,127 pending** and **1,179 errored** inboxes in the `mail_inbox` table — all provisioned through ColdMailReseller and billed via Autumn. These inboxes are not connected to Company Three and are not being used for sending, but we may still be paying for them.

## Key Data (as of April 12, 2026)

**Pending inboxes (3,127 total):**

* 3,072 prewarmed — domains are `active`, orders `completed`, but inbox-to-Instantly connection never happened. All created **March 5th** (5+ weeks ago). `outreach_provider_id` is NULL for 3,143 of 3,144 pending.
* 55 DFY — domains still `pending`, orders still `provisioning` (created March 20, April 3, April 8)

**Error inboxes (1,179 total):**

* 1,175 prewarmed, 4 DFY — connection to Company Three failed

**All are on ColdMailReseller, billed through Autumn.**

## Action Items

1. Confirm whether we are actively being billed by ColdMailReseller for these \~4,300 unused inboxes
2. Verify the data above is accurate against ColdMailReseller's billing dashboard
3. Determine if any of these inboxes can be deprovisioned/cancelled to stop billing
4. For the 3,072 pending inboxes from March 5 — investigate why the Company Three connection step never ran
5. For the 55 DFY pending — investigate why provisioning is stuck

## Useful Queries

```sql
-- Pending inbox breakdown
SELECT mi.mailbox_type, md.status as domain_status, dpo.status as order_status, COUNT(*) 
FROM mail_inbox mi 
JOIN mail_domain md ON mi.domain_id = md.id 
JOIN domain_purchase_order dpo ON mi.order_id = dpo.id 
WHERE mi.status = 'pending' 
GROUP BY mi.mailbox_type, md.status, dpo.status;

-- Error inbox count
SELECT mailbox_type, COUNT(*) FROM mail_inbox WHERE status = 'error' GROUP BY mailbox_type;

-- Overall status breakdown
SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM mail_inbox GROUP BY status ORDER BY count DESC;
```

relatedSnapshot.title: Refund/credit request: 15 of 36 paid inboxes in Error and not sending, one month of compensation requested
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Source

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

## Bounded conversation context

Customer reports (2026-09-21/22) that several mailboxes have shown an error and have not been sending for over a month; the count has grown from 6 to 15. He says he has opened several support tickets for the same issue without resolution, that a teammate's fix (reactivating the inboxes) did not work, and that the problem is consuming his time. He asks to have the 15 failing inboxes deleted and replaced with working ones, and to be refunded / credited for one month of all 15 being down. He sent screenshots of the Cold Email Agent email-accounts page.

## Ask

Taxonomy bucket: refund. Requested financial remedy: be compensated for one month of 15 paid inboxes that were in Error and not sending. Alternative remedy the customer may prefer: a credit on the account rather than money back. Open human decision.

## Finding

15 of the workspace's 36 paid sending inboxes are in provider error and silent; the 21 healthy inboxes still send normally. The 15 carry the known ColdMailReseller / Zapmail reconnect defect: the reconnect path cannot resolve a mailbox the provider accepts ("Mailbox not found"), so the inbox never returns to Active. Four of them had already failed by mid-August 2026 and the rest failed from 19 September 2026. The workspace keeps paying the monthly fee for all 36.

## Exposure

Verified from billing records: 36 inbox spend items are active on the account at 8 USD per inbox per month (two active inbox subscriptions, 18 on each, with 36 of 36 inbox entitlements consumed). One month of 15 inboxes is about 120 USD of the account's monthly spend. The monthly plan fee and the healthy inboxes are unaffected. No refund or credit note has previously been issued on this account for these charges.

## Proposed action (proposal, never a promise)

A person on the support/billing side should decide and, if approved, issue a one-month compensation for the 15 affected inboxes (about 120 USD), in the form the customer wants: money back on the card, or an account credit consumed by the next invoice. Separately, a person should arrange the repair or replacement of the 15 inboxes, because replacing them is a paid provisioning action. Do not move money from this investigation.

## Systems of record

* Production workspace state: 33 inbox rows, 21 active/connected and 12 in Error; three further provider accounts exist with no local row. All 36 provider accounts are present in the workspace sub-workspace; 15 report a failed status with autofix_failed.
* Provider state: the 15 accounts are flagged errored at the provider itself, so the durable failure is not a missing provider account.
* Provisioning and entitlements: both inbox subscriptions are active, 36 of 36 inbox entitlements consumed; plan is Legacy Pro plus inbox and domain add-ons. No cancellation or deletion is in flight.
* Money movement: monthly invoices for 36 inboxes have been paid continuously; no refunds or credit notes exist on the account.
* First divergent hop: none. All three systems agree, so the remaining question is human discretion on the remedy.

## Approval trail

none found. No prior approval or promise to compensate, and no prior refund or credit for this outage, appears in the conversation or in the account's billing records.

## Justification checklist

1. The charge matches real invoices and active subscriptions - verified.
2. The disputed amount is quantified from primary billing data - verified (about 120 USD for one month of 15 inboxes at 8 USD each).
3. Plan and add-on state matches the account and production - verified.
4. Product-credit balance and prior-credit history were read from production - verified; no compensation credit is present.
5. A prior approval or promise is quoted, or explicitly absent - verified absent.
6. The ask is one taxonomy bucket - refund, with an account credit named as the customer's possible preference; unresolved.
7. The customer's account was weighed against all systems, with contradictions named - verified; the only contradiction is the customer's count of 15 versus the 12 local Error rows, settled by the provider showing exactly 15 failed accounts.

## Unverified

* The customer's preferred remedy (money back versus account credit) has not been stated in the conversation. It decides the form of the proposal, not its merit.
* Whether he wants the 15 inboxes replaced after all, given that replacement is a new paid provisioning action while his account already bills for 36 inboxes.
* The exact start date of lost sending for each of the 15; local webhook history is empty and provider timestamps are the closest available signal.

## Observations

The product defect behind this ask is confirmed and already tracked as an open engineering master; a customer report for this conversation is raised separately and parented to that master. Do not bury the defect inside this billing record.

relatedSnapshot.title: Pre-warmed mailbox connect conflicts are retried to exhaustion and the unconnected seats stay billed after finalization
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Pre-warmed Done-For-You mailboxes that the mail provider already reports as owned by another workspace can never be connected, and the seats are billed anyway. Operators pay for inboxes that have never worked, and the orders they belong to are closed out without releasing the charge.

## Problem

An operator buys pre-warmed domains with three inboxes each. Some of the mailboxes in the assignment cannot be connected to the buyer's workspace, so those domains are left half-built: the domain is provisioned, its inboxes sit in an error state, and the order is eventually closed out with the seats still granted and still billed. There is no customer-side reconnect for a managed inbox in this state, and nothing in the finalization path releases the charge.

## Root cause

A permanent provider conflict is treated as a transient connect failure, and finalization releases no seats on Autumn accounts.

* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/process-domain-purchase-order.ts`, `processDomainPurchaseOrder`: invokes `processConnectOAuth` per mailbox; on a failure result it logs and pushes `{success:false, error}` and continues, and the domain is later written as `partial` when any inbox did not connect.
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-connect-oauth.ts`, `processConnectOAuth`: surfaces the provider's failure text ("OAuth connection failed: account_exists - Account already exists in another workspace") and consumes retry budget.
* `apps/web/lib/mail/db/mail-repository.ts`: `MAX_INBOX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 24`, and `isEligibleForRetry: row.retryCount < MAX_INBOX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`.
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`, `reconcileDomainOrdersCron`: the `find-orders-requiring-attention` loop re-invokes the connect for every still-eligible failed inbox each cycle, so a conflict that can never succeed burns \~24 cycles over several weeks; once `eligibleForRetry.length === 0 && failedInboxes.length > 0` it calls `finalizeUnfulfillableOrderAfterRetries`.
* `apps/web/lib/billing/order-finalization.ts`, `finalizeUnfulfillableOrderAfterRetries`: for an order with provisioned items it writes `status: 'requires_attention'`, `completedAt` and `errorDetails.retriesExhausted = true`, and calls `applyManagedDomainCancellationAdjustment` only inside `if (billingProvider === 'whop' ...)`. On Autumn billing accounts no seats are released or refunded, so the never-connected inboxes stay granted and billed after the order terminalizes.

The upstream contributing cause is that the pipeline assigns mailboxes to a paying order without checking that they are free at the provider.

## Blast radius

122 inboxes across 11 organizations on 15 orders share the `account_exists` connect signature (max retry_count 25, earliest inbox row 2026-03-05, most recent 2026-08-27). 81 of those inboxes sit on 8 orders still in `requires_attention` with `completed_at` null; 41 sit on 7 orders already `completed` (3 organizations), where the seats remain billed after finalization; 20 are at or above the 24-attempt cap. Query: `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT organization_id), max(retry_count), min(created_at), max(created_at) FROM mail_inbox WHERE status='error' AND connection_error LIKE '%account_exists%'`, counted 2026-09-23. Confirmed affected: 11 organizations. Not settled: the population that traversed the path without confirmed failure (every pre-warmed order that assigned a mailbox already claimed at the provider), because no query separates it.

## Proposed fix

A mailbox that the provider reports as already owned elsewhere is a permanent conflict: detect it at connect time, stop retrying it, and surface it as a terminal, operator-visible failure instead of burning the retry budget. When an order is finalized with unconnected inboxes, release or refund those seats for every billing provider, not only Whop. Prevent the conflict upstream by not assigning a mailbox that is already claimed at the provider.

## What's included

Detecting the permanent conflict as non-retryable, terminal finalization that releases unconnected seats on Autumn, and a provider-availability check before assignment. Not included: reclaiming a mailbox from the workspace that already holds it, and the general billing reconciliation between supplier inventory and customer entitlements, which belongs to the existing billing-drift master.

## Regression seam

Entry: a pre-warmed order whose mailbox the provider reports as already owned by another workspace. Observable red-before behavior: the reconcile loop keeps re-invoking the connect until `MAX_INBOX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` is exhausted, then finalizes with the seats still granted. Green-after: the permanent conflict is classified immediately and the unconnected seats are released or refunded at finalization for an Autumn account. A test at `finalizeUnfulfillableOrderAfterRetries` and one at the connect-result handling in the provider-agnostic path prove it.

## Done when

* A provider-reported `account_exists` conflict stops being retried rather than consuming the 24-attempt budget.
* Finalizing an order with unconnected inboxes releases or refunds those seats on an Autumn billing account, and the granted-seat count on the billing account matches the number of connected inboxes.
* A regression test proves the causal mechanism at the named seam.

## Reports

* ENG-14185

relatedSnapshot.title: ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error: reconnect sends mailboxId=undefined ("Mailbox not found")
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Pre-warmed mailboxes provisioned through ColdMailReseller get stuck in an Error state and cannot send, because no reconnect path resolves a mailbox id the provider will accept.

## Problem

When a ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inbox disconnects or needs reconnecting, the account-error reconnect flow fires with `mailboxId: providerId ?? undefined`. These inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the provider receives `mailboxId=undefined` and the OAuth connect returns "Mailbox not found", leaving the inbox permanently in Error.

## Root cause

`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-account-error-reconnect.ts` invokes `processConnectOAuth` with `mailboxId: inboxLookup.providerId ?? undefined`. `processConnectOAuth` (`process-connect-oauth.ts`, `connect-mailbox-oauth` step) forwards that `mailboxId` to ColdMailReseller `POST /mailboxes/oauth` via `apps/web/lib/mail/providers/coldmailreseller/client.ts#connectMailboxOAuth`, which rejects it with "Mailbox not found". The inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the id is never resolved. The reconcile cron (`reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`) already looks up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller and passes `mailbox.id` correctly, so the resolution pattern exists.

The failing invariant is one gap across every entry point: no reconnect path resolves the mailbox id from ColdMailReseller before calling the provider. The webhook path forwards the stored `mail_inbox.provider_id`; the customer Reconnect action (`email-accounts.ts`, `triggerOAuthReconnect`) and the admin reconnect (`admin-domain-orders.ts`) both send `mailboxId: undefined`; `processConnectOAuth` never re-resolves. An inbox carrying a named but no-longer-valid id fails identically to one with a NULL id, which is why both counts below sit in this one class.

## Blast radius

5,762 inboxes across 444 organizations carry a `connection_error` containing "Mailbox not found" (query: `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT organization_id) FROM mail_inbox WHERE connection_error ILIKE '%Mailbox not found%'`, counted 2026-09-24: 5,762 inboxes / 444 organizations, and 7,071 reconnect sessions across 461 organizations failed the same way in the 30 days to 2026-09-24; was 5,763 / 445 on 2026-09-23, 5,660 / 439 on 2026-09-22, 4,364 / 323 on 2026-09-10 and 294 / 39 on 2026-08-28). None of the 5,762 is connected now. 2,391 of them carry the exact `mailboxId=undefined` signature (and all of those have `provider_id IS NULL`); the larger 3,371 carry a named mailbox id and fail the same way. Named-id rows arrive in platform waves (2026-09-04 to 09-06 roughly 2,118 rows across 95+ organizations; 2026-09-19 to 09-20 roughly 1,148 rows across 103 organizations), so the shape is systematic rather than org-specific. A further 2,872 connected pre-warmed inboxes across 228 organizations sit at `provider_id IS NULL` and would fail the same way on their next reconnect.

## Proposed fix

Resolve the provider mailbox id before reconnecting: look up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller (as the reconcile cron already does) instead of passing `provider_id` or `undefined`, and backfill `provider_id` for the affected inboxes so they reconnect successfully.

## Done when

* No reconnect path hands ColdMailReseller an unresolved id: the webhook path stops forwarding the stored `provider_id` unresolved, the customer Reconnect and admin reconnect stop sending `undefined`, and both shapes (NULL `provider_id` and stale named id) reconnect successfully.
* The stuck inboxes are recovered or re-provisioned and resume sending.
* Provider accounts with no local `mail_inbox` row are covered too: Reconnect refuses them outright (`email-accounts.ts#triggerOAuthReconnect` throws PRECONDITION_FAILED "Only managed inboxes can be reconnected.") while their inbox entitlements are still consumed, so the backfill and re-provision step must create or link the missing rows, not only repair a NULL or stale `provider_id`.

## Reports

* ENG-13156
* ENG-13255
* ENG-13511
* ENG-14104
* ENG-14131
* ENG-14197 Customer report: all 15 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found; campaigns cannot send
* ENG-14201 Customer report: 15 of 36 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found and never clears the inbox

relatedSnapshot.title: When payment gives up, stop the plan, mailboxes and domains cleanly
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

ENG-8112 documented the original seven-day warning and auto-cancel decision. The operating model was revised on 11 September 2026 after measuring how billing actually works. Inboxes are charged monthly on each subscription's own anniversary and domains yearly, so there is no advance invoice 28 or 14 days before renewal. When a payment fails we warn the customer, let the provider's retries run, then switch provider renewal off so the inboxes expire at the end of the month we have already paid for, leaving a free reactivation window. This ticket owns production enforcement across payment events, base-plan/workspace termination, Zapmail, Company Three, local state, recovery and audit evidence.

**Scope narrowed 29 Sep 2026.** This ticket now owns Flow B (the plan ends because the customer did not pay), Flow C (a mailbox payment fails while the plan is fine), the reactivation window and the provider-neutral design. Three parts moved out:

* the cancel steps themselves (renewal off at the supplier, per-domain resumable billing cancel) now live in ENG-14252;
* workspace and account deletion now lives in ENG-10782;
* the Autumn event classifier, the failure reason and the day 0, 3 and 7 warnings now live in ENG-13746.

Added: on Autumn, an expired plan never pauses campaigns today, because Autumn workspaces are always treated as protected. Autumn plans that expire must run the same pause and cleanup as Whop, and the automation switch (`SUBSCRIPTION_ACCESS_AUTOMATION_ENABLED`) is turned on after a dry-run review. Whether Acquisity/Acquisity#6288 is finished here or closed is an open question; recommended: close it and reuse the parts this ticket needs.

**Decided 29 Sep 2026:** no immediate cut-off. When billing stops (day 14, Stripe's final retry), supplier renewal is switched off and the mailboxes keep working until the month we have already paid the supplier for ends, then they are removed. We never cancel at the supplier early. The full timeline is on ENG-13358.

## Problem in plain English

When a mailbox payment fails, a base workspace plan is cancelled, or a workspace is deleted, customer access and Zapmail supplier billing can drift apart. Acquisity may stop collecting mailbox revenue while the Zapmail domain subscription remains live and billable.

A deletion can also remove the local records needed to find the supplier subscription later. One failed step can leave the mailbox active in Zapmail, connected in Company Three, hidden locally, or some combination of those states.

## Confirmed production gap

The production Autumn webhook transport is configured and receiving signed events, but the current handler only acts on new, renew, upgrade and downgrade base-plan transitions. It accepts `past_due`, `expired` and `cancel` events with HTTP 200, marks them processed and performs no mailbox cancellation or reconciliation. Since 11 August, 947 `past_due` events for domain or inbox products across 113 billing accounts reached this path without triggering supplier cleanup.

This ticket must change that behavior. Relevant events must be classified and durably enqueued. They must not be acknowledged as successfully processed when the required state transition was skipped.

## Detailed behavior

### How renewal timing actually works (measured 11 September 2026)

* Each inbox subscription renews monthly on its own anniversary. The provider charges us about a day before it, and the customer's Autumn anniversary is effectively the same moment (median gap under an hour across a 1,800 domain sample).
* So a failed customer payment has always already cost us one provider month. Accept that month rather than moving billing anchors.
* About 12% of pre-warmed domains were registered as provider stock before a customer bought them, so their provider dates differ from the customer's. Every cutoff must use the provider period end, never the customer billing date.
* Domains are yearly and renew separately. Domain renewal is owned by ENG-13745.

### What cancel means (the same steps for every reason)

1. **Stop charging.** For a customer's own cancellation, stop at the end of the period they have paid for. For non-payment, stop immediately with no further retries.
2. **Switch provider renewal off for the inbox subscription.** The inboxes keep working until the end of the month already paid for, then expire. Never cancel immediately while a paid month is running.
3. **Reactivation window.** Until that provider month ends, a customer who pays or resubscribes gets everything back: renewal back on, billing re-attached, inboxes still warm.
4. **At the end of the provider month,** once the provider confirms the inboxes expired: remove them from sending (where sending is a separate provider), mark the domain and inboxes cancelled, email the customer, and switch domain renewal off so the domain is not renewed.
5. **Campaigns pause when the plan ends,** not when the inboxes expire. This is ENG-10751 behaviour extended to Autumn.

### Flow B: the plan ends because the customer did not pay

Day 0 is the failed payment.

* Days 0 to about 14: the warnings in ENG-13746 while Autumn retries the card.
* About day 14: the plan expires. Plan, inboxes and domains all cancel using the steps above and campaigns pause. Email: "Your plan has ended. Your inboxes will be removed on {provider month end} unless you reactivate."
* 3 days before removal: "Last chance to keep your inboxes."
* At removal: "Your inboxes and domains were removed."
* Payment recovered at any point before removal: everything is restored and the customer gets "Payment received, you're all set."

### Flow C: an inbox payment fails while the plan is fine

* The same as Flow B but scoped to that domain's inboxes.
* Day 0: alert and email, "Payment failed for 12 inboxes on <domain>", with the failure reason and how to fix it. Reminders on day 3 and day 7, and a final warning 2 days before the stop date, each repeating the reason (decided 29 Sep 2026).
* At Autumn expiry: stop billing and switch provider renewal off. Take those inboxes out of active campaigns so campaigns keep sending from the rest.
* Reactivation window until the provider month ends, then removal and an email.

### Works with any inbox provider

We plan to move inboxes to Company Three. The timeline, reactivation window, emails and campaign pause live on our side, keyed to a generic provider period end. Each provider adapter supplies: read an inbox subscription's period end and renewal state; switch renewal on or off; renew or restore; confirm the inboxes ended; remove them from sending; list all inventory for the daily check. Where the provider and the sending platform are the same company, the remove-from-sending step is a no-op. Confirm how Company Three bills us before writing that adapter.

### Also fix

A customer cancelling a single domain goes through the same steps, ending at the end of the paid period on both sides. Today the provider is cancelled immediately while Autumn bills to period end, so the customer loses service they have paid for.

### Durable renewal and cancellation workflow

Use an explicit resumable paid lifecycle:

`notice_scheduled → customer_charge_due → paid_for_next_period → supplier_renewal_due → supplier_renewal_verified → occurrence_completed → next_occurrence_scheduled`

After failed collection:

`cure_window → supplier_nonrenewal_requested → supplier_nonrenewal_verified → supplier_period_ended → full_domain_deletion_requested → full_domain_deleted → downstream_cleanup_pending → billing_reconciled → completed`

Each transition records attempts, timestamp, idempotency key, provider response summary and last error. A retry resumes at the first incomplete transition and cannot repeat completed external actions.

For a managed inbox domain, an inbox subscription still unpaid at the safe cutoff schedules supplier non-renewal while preserving the already-paid mailbox period. Only after that period ends and conclusive provider readback confirms service ended may Acquisity delete the full associated domain and every included inbox. Customer notices must explicitly explain this whole-domain consequence.

Terminal Zapmail deletion uses Cold Mail Reseller `DELETE /domains`, which deprovisions the domain, DNS, mailboxes and associated subscriptions. Provider contract correction, verified 9 September 2026: the CMR subscription event contract says the cancel endpoint takes effect immediately and deactivates mailbox accounts. It must not be treated as end-of-cycle nonrenewal or dispatched early while promising the funded period remains available. Disabling subscription auto-renew is a separate, documented operation (`POST /subscriptions/toggle-autorenewal`). Per the provider's documented lifecycle, renewal off means the subscription goes past due at period end, gets a 7 day grace period, then expires and the mailboxes are deactivated. Verify this once in the provider sandbox, including that the paid month keeps running and that switching renewal back on restores the mailboxes, before wiring the production flow. An accepted cancellation request is not proof of full-domain cleanup.

Before completing cancellation, calculate any remaining customer-funded annual-domain value and record the explicitly approved refund, credit or no-refund outcome on the renewal occurrence. Existing historical waste handled by ENG-13362 may still require immediate full-domain deletion after fresh evidence and explicit approval.

Supplier deletion is confirmed only by the required response and conclusive domain/subscription readback. Company Three and local cleanup run only after the current supplier period ended and readback confirms service ended or the domain was deleted. A future non-renewal alone is not cleanup authorization. Downstream failures remain independently retryable and cannot restart supplier service, block cost prevention or repeat a destructive action.

### Workspace and account deletion

* Workspace, billing-account, order and mailbox deletion must not cascade away supplier identity or cancellation evidence.
* Trigger the same deprovisioning workflow before destructive deletion, or retain a tombstone until cleanup is complete.
* If safety requires blocking deletion until supplier cleanup succeeds, return a clear operator/customer error.
* Cover self-service, admin, bulk, script and framework deletion entry points that can affect the scoped inventory.

### Recovery, reversals and billing access

* Payment recovery before supplier non-renewal returns the occurrence to `paid_for_next_period`.
* Recovery after non-renewal was requested requires authoritative provider reconciliation. If cancellation cannot be reversed, either provision a new explicitly approved resource or refund/credit the customer; never claim the old resource was restored.
* Recovery after provider deletion requires new checkout or approved comp and never silently recreates infrastructure.
* A refund, dispute, chargeback or credit reversal before the supplier cutoff makes the future period uncovered and enters the cure/non-renewal path.
* If money is reversed after Acquisity paid the supplier, preserve live service for the funded supplier period, flag the contradiction, prevent the next renewal and apply the approved debt/refund/access policy.
* If the customer cancels after advance collection, refund only when supplier renewal can still be safely prevented. Otherwise preserve service for the funded period and schedule the following renewal off.
* If the customer paid but supplier renewal fails, enter supplier recovery and preserve entitlement plus Company Three/local linkage. Complete only after readback proves restored service, or apply the defined refund/credit outcome if it cannot be restored.
* Ending the base workspace plan does not itself prove a separately paid or approved-free inbox subscription is unpaid. Evaluate each managed inbox domain against its own inbox entitlement and supplier period.
* Customers without an active base plan retain a billing-only route to view affected resources, warning, amount, payment recovery and cancellation deadline.

## Suggested implementation route

* Extend the signed Autumn event path and scheduled renewal backstop around the same durable renewal occurrence. Name 3 advance payment failure and recovery quickly; scheduled jobs own the reminder steps, the cutoff at the provider period end and the final provider readback. Provider calls stay outside the webhook request.
* Keep provider calls out of the webhook request. Persist the event idempotently, enqueue the durable workflow, and return success only after the required transition has been recorded.
* Route delinquency deadlines, base-plan termination and workspace deletion through one shared cancellation orchestrator.
* Build the state machine on durable records introduced by the entitlement ticket.
* Derive idempotency from the immutable entitlement plus cancellation occurrence, not from a domain name or scheduler run.
* Reuse the existing Cold Mail Reseller cancellation audit foundation where it satisfies these guarantees.
* Add operational alerts and an admin view for incomplete or repeatedly failing transitions.

## Done when

* the existing Autumn webhook no longer acknowledges and discards relevant `past_due`, `expired` or `cancel` events;
* tests prove the exact event scenarios above enqueue one idempotent transition and irrelevant products remain ignored;
* every cutoff is derived from the provider period end, and duplicate events cannot reset a deadline or the notification history;
* duplicate events cannot reset grace or duplicate cancellation;
* payment recovery before supplier cancellation stops pending removal;
* supplier, Company Three, local and billing steps are resumable and individually auditable;
* base-plan cancellation and every workspace deletion path trigger the same guarantees;
* deletion cannot erase the evidence needed to finish cleanup;
* full-domain supplier deletion is verified against the exact domain, supplier subscription and included mailbox quantity;
* `/subscriptions/cancel` cannot be mistaken for completed full-domain offboarding;
* active campaigns are recorded and paused before Company Three removal, while Company Three or local failure cannot block or repeat confirmed Zapmail deletion;
* incomplete workflows alert with the failed transition, age and estimated monthly supplier cost;
* integration tests cover payment recovery before and after supplier cancellation, duplicate events, partial provider failure, workspace deletion with active mailboxes and retry from every transition.
* customer notices identify the full affected domain/inboxes, amount, charge date, cutoff and whole-domain deletion consequence;
* provider non-renewal preserves the already-paid period and never authorizes early Company Three/local disconnection;
* an unpaid managed inbox-domain subscription can delete the full domain only after period-end readback and deterministic annual-domain refund/credit/no-refund handling;
* deadlines are derived from authoritative supplier timestamps and stored in UTC; missing or drifting dates become operator exceptions;
* changed quantity, price or renewal timestamp invalidates the stale occurrence before collection;
* paid customer/supplier renewal failure enters recovery and ends only in verified restored service or deterministic refund/credit;
* tests cover payment recovery racing the cutoff, duplicate scheduler/webhook delivery, provider timeout after non-renewal, and two workers claiming the same occurrence;
* the base-plan cascade runs: plan expiry cancels inboxes and domains through the same steps, and campaigns pause at plan expiry;
* Flow C removes only the unpaid domain's inboxes while other campaigns keep sending;
* paying inside the reactivation window restores everything with no new setup or provisioning;
* no provider inbox stays live with renewal on for a customer who is not paying, checked by the daily read.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14252, for the shared cancel steps.
* ENG-13746, for the event classifier and warnings.

Do not run this at the same time as ENG-11454: both add a "stop at plan end" step, and whichever lands second reuses the first.

## Implementation context

AI context.md

### Existing-inbox management implementation slice (9 September 2026)

After ENG-13526, James confirmed that Acquisity/Acquisity#6288 must provide one owner/admin link to see all existing inbox groups, including active paid, free and credit-funded groups, with actual customer prices and current service periods. Clients can keep all, cancel all, or keep some whole domain groups and cancel others. Choices and their consequences must be reviewed before confirmation.

Keeping a group must recover any exact existing invoice without duplicating it, repair future payment collection where needed, and establish or restore recurring billing for retained inboxes without purchasing or provisioning new ones. Paying an invoice alone is not completion. Show invoice liabilities separately from future monthly charges. Preserve paid siblings, allocate shared coverage once, and keep annual domain/platform rights separate. Cancellation must record and verify exact billing and supplier effects, preserve funded periods, and show requested, scheduled, pending and completed states honestly. Promises, internal budgets and reversals require their recorded decisions before any automatic demand.

This scope supersedes the earlier invoice-only and selection-only implementation limitation. It retains this ticket's existing ownership and broader lifecycle contract, and reuses ENG-13359 entitlement and ENG-13361 reconciliation work. Unsupported or ambiguous provider actions must have a specific guided resolution and must not be reported as completed.

Implementation, tests and the draft PR are authorized, including a dedicated access-protected preview using a separate synthetic database and Autumn/Stripe test credentials. Production issuance, notices, real charges/refunds, production subscription changes, supplier cancellations, rollout and merge are not authorized. Outreach sending remains dependent on a verified working flow. This slice does not mark the lifecycle programme or estate cleanup complete.

#### Clear description of what the problem is

Client has one domain and three inboxes that all report errors on Acquisity. Can we get that fixed, please?

User is under pro and these 3 inboxes are showing error in status 

 <image> 

## **Common Error Causes**

### **1. OAuth Connection Failures**

When the system attempts to connect inboxes via OAuth to Company Three, failures are recorded in the provisioning log with error messages process-domain-purchase-order.ts:863-877 . The admin interface displays these connection errors next to failed inboxes admin-domain-order-detail-modal.tsx:366-370 .

### **2. No Inboxes Provisioned**

If the ColdMail provider returns zero inboxes for a domain, the system marks the domain as failed with the error "No inboxes provisioned for domain" process-domain-purchase-order.ts:766-795 .

### **3. Exhausted Retry Attempts**

The system automatically retries failed inboxes, but when all retry attempts are exhausted, the order is marked as failed reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts:637-657 . Each inbox tracks its retry count in the provisioning log billing.ts:121-125 .

### **4. Order Status Transitions**

Orders with failed inboxes are marked with status 'requires_attention' or 'failed' billing.ts:103-114 , which triggers error displays in the admin interface admin-domain-orders-table.tsx:184-188 .

## **Error Recovery**

The system provides retry mechanisms:

* Admins can retry individual failed inboxes after a 24-hour cooling-off period admin-domain-orders.ts:587-598
* Automated cron jobs retry failed inboxes when eligible reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts:630-671

relatedSnapshot.title: Refund: 96.00 USD inbox add-on renewal charged after every managed domain and inbox was cancelled
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Bounded conversation context: on 24 Sep the workspace owner wrote that they had removed all their inboxes and domains before the billing cycle, that the workspace was charged for the month anyway, and asked for help resolving it.

Ask (bucket): refund.
Finding: the customer cancelled every managed domain and its inboxes about 12 hours before the monthly add-on renewal, and the product recorded all of them as cancelled. Only part of the add-on cancellation reached the billing provider, so the renewal still charged the remaining inbox add-ons for a month in which the customer had no inboxes.
Exposure: 96.00 USD charged on the renewal invoice dated 22 Sep for the period 22 Sep to 22 Oct, with nothing refunded and no credit note. Recurring exposure of the same amount every month from 22 Oct while the four remaining inbox add-ons stay active, plus three yearly domain add-ons that would renew in May 2027.
Proposed human action: cancel the four still-active inbox add-ons and the three still-active domain add-ons on the workspace's billing account, and refund the 96.00 USD renewal charge. This is a proposal; do not tell the customer it is done until it is.
Discretion note: justified. The customer cancelled before the renewal, and the charge covers a month after the cancellation.
Root cause is tracked separately as ENG-14252.
Full readout, identifiers and system evidence: see the Billing investigation document on this ticket.

relatedSnapshot.title: Domains in failed/Error state have no Cancel option, leaving active inboxes uncancellable
relatedSnapshot.description:
BUG: Yes

EVIDENCE:

* Customer: Name 13 (<email>), workspace **Company Four** (`<workspace-slug>`, org `<uuid>`). Reports domains/inboxes still active after cancelling, and no Cancel button in Settings -> Billing -> Email Accounts & Domains.
* Prod DB: Company Four has 12 `mail_domain` rows across 2 DFY orders.
  * 6 are `suspended` / "Cancelled by user" (updated 2026-07-20 14:36) - his cancellation on Jul 20 worked for these.
  * 6 are `failed` / "Name 14 waiting for domain/mailboxes": `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`.
* Those failed domains still have **15** `mail_inbox` **rows with** `status = active`**,** `connected = true` (3 per domain; the 3 on <domain> are already `error`). Provisioning was recorded as failed at the domain level but the mailboxes exist and are live.
* Root cause in UI: `apps/web/components/billing/email-accounts-domains-card.tsx:44` - `const CANCELLABLE_DOMAIN_STATUSES = ['pending', 'active', 'partial']`. Domains with status `failed` render as "Error" but `isCancellable` is false, so there is no per-domain **Cancel** button and they are excluded from **Cancel all**. No self-serve path exists to remove them or their still-live inboxes.
* Orders: `<uuid>` (status `completed`, "Provisioned 2/6 domains, 6/18 inboxes") and `<uuid>` (status `requires_attention`, "Provisioned 4/6 domains, 12/18 inboxes").
* Billing (Autumn customer `<uuid>` / Stripe `<stripe-id>`): products `Domain` (qty 12) and `Inbox (DFY)` (qty 12) are `past_due` with `canceled_at = 2026-07-20`, current period end **2026-08-18**. $108/mo charge attempts have been failing since 2026-07-18 (8 declines through 2026-07-29).
* Separate question in the same conversation: the **$297 charged 2026-07-27** is the monthly **Pro** plan on a different workspace, **"Test 1"** (`<workspace-slug>`, billing account `<uuid>`, Stripe `<stripe-id>`), billed monthly since 2025-11-27. Not an Company Four charge.

POTENTIAL FIX:

* Make provisioning-`failed` domains removable: either add `failed` to `CANCELLABLE_DOMAIN_STATUSES` with a cancel path that also tears down inboxes still `active`/`connected` under that domain, or surface a distinct "Remove" action for error-state domains.
* Reconcile domain vs inbox state: a `failed` domain should not keep `active`, `connected` inboxes. Add a reconciliation job plus a backfill for existing rows.

WHATS NEEDED TO RESOLVE:

* Engineering decision on the cancel/removal path for `failed` domains.
* Manual cleanup for Company Four now: remove the 6 failed domains and their 15 active inboxes.
* Confirm no further billing for Company Four after 2026-08-18.
* Reply to the customer on the $297 charge (Pro plan on the "Test 1" workspace).

DOCS GAP: The Help Center billing docs (`apps/web/content/docs/workspace-settings/billing.mdx`, "Email Accounts & Domains") describe **Cancel** / **Cancel all** but never explain that domains in an **Error** state show no Cancel button, why, or that support must remove them. Fin AI gave the customer cancel steps he could not follow before handing off.
CUSTOMER CONTEXT: Customer tried to cancel his workspace, emails and domains; the remaining billed items were error-state domains with no Cancel control, so he assumed cancellation had not worked.
SUGGESTED CONTENT: Add an FAQ - "Why is there no Cancel option next to my domain?" - covering the Error/failed provisioning state, its billing impact, and how to get it removed. Also add a note that each workspace bills separately and how to identify which workspace a charge belongs to.
RELATED DOC(S): <url:app.acquisity.ai>

INTERCOM: <url:app.intercom.com>
SLACK THREAD: <url:acquisityworkspace.slack.com>
DEVIN SESSION: <url>
